title: Docs site: refresh staging + canary publishing playbook (routes, checks, rollback)
author: Mariana Liu
description: Context: The Confluence playbook "Docs site content staging and canary publishing playbook" is now out of date. Since the Feb game-day we changed (a) staging to PR Preview Environments, (b) canary routing from edge rules to the docs-router service, and (c) our acceptance thresholds and smoke suite ownership. This PR refreshes the playbook in-repo and adds a small "runbook" appendix for the oncall. Goal: reduce rollback latency and eliminate ambiguity about which commands/URLs are current. Summary of updates (what changed vs the old playbook): 1) Environments: Staging is no longer a single long-lived site. We now use per-PR preview envs. The shared environment is "preprod" (formerly called staging) and is only used for final integration checks. URLs now: - PR Preview: https://pr-<number>.preview.docs.redwood.com (created automatically on PRs) - Preprod: https://preprod.docs.redwood.com - Prod: https://docs.redwood.com 2) Canary routing: We no longer use ad-hoc CDN edge rules. Traffic shifting is done via docs-router (Envoy) weights and a cookie override for debugging. Canary commands updated to the new deploy wrapper (docsctl) and router config. 3) Acceptance criteria: Tightened thresholds based on incident review: - Server 5xx for canary cohort must be < 0.05% (was 0.1%) over the 30 min window - Client JS exception rate delta must be < 10% (was 20%) - p95 render time delta must be < 10% (was 15%) - Added explicit "broken anchors / sidebar nav" check in CI 4) Canary ramp schedule: Standardized to 1% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with specific dwell times, and an optional "internal-only" ramp via the employee login gate for large rewrites. 5) Rollback: Rollback now uses pinned content artifact IDs rather than "previous-stable" (which was ambiguous after the artifact retention change). Added explicit command to fetch the last good artifact and a note about router weights during rollback. 6) Smoke tests: Split into "fast" (CI) and "live" (preprod/prod) and clarified owners. Snippet runner now runs against the "docs-sandbox" backend (not staging inference). Included updated paths for the snippet harness. Checklist for authors: - Pages modified (list) - SDKs impacted (list) - Smoke test IDs to run (fast/live) - Rollback plan (artifact ID strategy) - Observability links (dashboards) - Requires SRE signoff? (yes/no) Commands (new): - Deploy canary: docsctl deploy --env=prod --mode=canary --weight=1 --artifact=pr:<PR_NUMBER> - Increase weight: docsctl canary set-weight --env=prod --weight=10 (etc) - Rollback to artifact: docsctl deploy --env=prod --mode=rollback --artifact=<artifact_id> - Override cookie for debugging: set "docs_canary=1" to force canary variant Acceptance thresholds (new): - Canary cohort 5xx < 0.05% over 30 min - Client JS exceptions delta < 10% vs baseline - p95 render time delta < 10% vs baseline - No increase in "snippet_exec_fail" rate above 0.2% absolute - No new "nav_link_404" errors in router logs above 5/min Rollout timing (new): - 1% for 20 min - 10% for 40 min - 25% for 40 min - 50% for 30 min - 100% then monitor 60 min + 24h passive watch Notes: This PR intentionally keeps most of the original structure and language so readers familiar with the Confluence version can diff quickly. Follow-ups: after merge we should (a) link the in-repo playbook from Confluence and (b) update #docs-release pinned message with the new docsctl commands.
commits: 1) docs(playbook): migrate environment model to PR previews + preprod (commit 8c2a9f1) 2) docs(playbook): update canary routing to docs-router and docsctl commands (commit 4bb1d23) 3) docs(playbook): tighten acceptance thresholds + add nav/anchor checks (commit 9d50e0c) 4) docs(runbook): add oncall appendix + rollback artifact guidance (commit 2a3d6f7)
conversation: Evan Patel (review): The switch from staging to preprod/preview is accurate. Can we be explicit that preview envs are the default for content review, and preprod is for integration only? Also, include the dashboard links so folks stop asking in #docs-release. Mariana Liu (author): Updated the Overview and added an Observability links include with the canonical dashboards + saved queries. Diego Morales (review): Rollback section: calling out "previous-stable" was confusing but artifact IDs are still hard for authors. Can we add a simple "how to find last-good artifact" snippet? Mariana Liu (author): Added docsctl artifacts list example and clarified retention (30 days) + which artifact to pick (last successful prod deploy). Sofia Ramirez (review): Acceptance thresholds: are we sure on JS exception delta < 10%? Some releases are noisy because of browser extensions. Maybe scope to our first-party bundle errors only? Hannah Kim (SRE review): +1. We should reference the "first_party" filter in the metric query and call that out in the playbook. Mariana Liu (author): Updated metric definition to use first_party=true and added the exact PromQL / dashboard panel name. Hannah Kim (SRE review): Canary ramp schedule: make 1% dwell 20 min (not 30) and require 10% dwell 40 min; aligns with router cache warmup behavior. Also please mention setting router weights back to 0 during rollback before re-deploying stable artifact. Mariana Liu (author): Done; added explicit step in rollback procedure. CI: Initially failed on markdown lint (trailing spaces) and link-check due to renamed dashboard URL; reran after fix. Final CI: docs-lint PASS, link-check PASS, snippet-fast PASS, build PASS, deploy-preview PASS. Approvals: Evan ✅ Diego ✅ Sofia ✅ Hannah ✅. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal docs playbook refresh: PR preview envs are now the default "staging" workflow; canary routing/commands updated to docs-router + docsctl; acceptance thresholds tightened; rollback now references explicit artifact IDs; added release oncall appendix.
content_source_note: Replaces/updates the older Confluence playbook content (last updated 2026-02-03) with current 2026-03 routing/CI/tooling. Confluence page should be treated as legacy once this is merged.
